newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to send home N.Korean sailor on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to send home N.Korean sailor on Tuesday.

text.p: South Korea will send home on Tuesday a North Korean sailor who was rescued while drifting off a southern island, a Seoul Defence Ministry spokesman said on Monday.
The sailor, Chung Kwang-son, private first class in North Korea's navy, would return home through the border village of Panmunjom, the spokesman said.
Chung, 19, was picked up by a South Korean maritime police vessel and taken to the western port city of Inchon on Saturday after his boat drifted south from North Korea.
He was first spotted on Friday about 21 miles (34 km) southwest of South Korea's So Yonpyongdo island, which is close to the border with the communist North, South Korean police said.

The return of Chung will be the first goodwill gesture by South Korea towards the North since tense relations between the two Koreas worsened after a Northern submarine landed 26 agents on a South Korean beach in September.
The ministry spokesman said the government had decided to honour Chung's wishes to go home on humanitarian grounds.

The U.S.-led United Nations Command will hand over Chung to North Korea at Panmunjom before representatives of the two sides discuss Pyongyang's demands to return the 24 bodies of North Korean agents killed in South Korea.
The 24 were among the 26 agents who landed in South Korea after their submarine ran aground off the eastern city of Kangnung. One was captured alive and another is still at large.
The North insists the September incident was an accident but Seoul wants an apology from the North, calling it a "grave provocation".

U.S. President Bill Clinton and South Korean leader Kim Young-sam urged North Korea on Sunday "to take acceptable steps to resolve the submarine incident, reduce tension and avoid such provocations in the future".
Their call was made after a meeting in the Philippines where both leaders are attending an annual summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.
